images.description: Steam in a game-console experience through nested Gamescope (legacy Big Picture, the games-on-whales-validated game-foreground path). Needs a host --shm-size bump, 32-bit graphics libraries, and PUID/PGID matching the managed home.
images.notes: no_new_privileges MUST be false: Steam's startup re-escalates via sudo inside the container, which the default --security-opt no-new-privileges blocks (black bare compositor otherwise). This knob rides apps.runtime_spec, not the runtime_presets columns — see MANIFEST.md 'runtime mapping'. network MUST be "bridge": Steam's first boot downloads steamui.so and clean-exits fatal under the hardened --network none default (first-run-experience spec §S2, #463) — this maps onto the runtime_presets.network column, hardened default stays "none" for every other image.

images.description: KDE Plasma 6 Wayland desktop session with the Steam desktop client, user-level Flatpak (Discover), and Quasar branding. Runs nested under the Quasar compositor; the whole mutable state lives in the /home/quasar volume (org.quasar.image.persist). Needs a host --shm-size bump and PUID/PGID matching the managed home, like Steam.
images.notes: no_new_privileges MUST be false: the bundled Steam desktop client's startup re-escalates via sudo, same as the steam image. network MUST be "bridge" (Steam sign-in/downloads). Desktop-session host requirements beyond the preset (agent-side, not yet preset-mappable): unprivileged user namespaces (seccomp permitting CLONE_NEWUSER — the agent's seccomp=unconfined covers it) AND unmasked /proc (--security-opt systempaths=unconfined) for user Flatpak's bwrap; without the latter flatpak install works but flatpak run fails mounting /proc (live-verified 2026-08-13). One running session per home volume (org.quasar.image.session=desktop).

images.description: UNIGINE Heaven 4.0 and Superposition 1.1 as a self-driving, looping GPU benchmark workload for Quasar streaming tests. Takes no input: the PHORONIX automation define runs the full scene sequence unattended, prints a score, exits, and the launcher restarts it. Bridges Quasar's Wayland session to the benchmarks' X11/GLX with stock gamescope.
images.notes: kind=template on purpose: the UNIGINE installers are ~1.9 GB of third-party downloads with their own EULAs, so this image is deliberately NOT published to ghcr and has no registry_ref to pin. Unlike steam/kde this image needs no security relaxations — no_new_privileges stays true and network stays none (the benchmarks are fully self-contained; the only network traffic is at BUILD time). Resolution is deliberately absent from env: the launcher takes the session mode from QUASAR_STREAM_WIDTH/HEIGHT (quasar#384), and a pinned UNIGINE_WIDTH/HEIGHT here would shadow it for every session. Results land in the managed home under ~/unigine-bench/run-<ts>/ and are also teed to stdout with a [unigine-result] prefix.

images.description: Deterministic native-Wayland Vulkan probe for measuring the streaming pipeline end to end. Every rendered frame carries a luma marker encoding its frame index, CLOCK_REALTIME submission time, scene, load and event flags, so a decoder running on the browser-received video can attribute each received frame to a rendered one. Five scenes of increasing codec difficulty (static, pan, swarm, flythrough, ui), a 0-10 GPU load dial, runtime control over a file or Unix socket, and per-frame JSONL telemetry in the managed home.
images.notes: kind=template like unigine-bench, but for a different reason: the payload is built from the unpublished quasar-benchgame repo, so `docker build -t quasar-benchapp:src .` must run there before ./scripts/build.sh quasar-benchapp here. This image deliberately carries NO gamescope/Xwayland — benchapp is a native Wayland client and a nested compositor would insert a second pacer and scaler into exactly the path being measured (verify-benchapp.sh asserts their absence). No security relaxations and no network: the probe is self-contained and makes no network calls. BENCHAPP_FPS and BENCHAPP_RENDER are deliberately absent from env: fps falls back to the session's QUASAR_STREAM_FPS, and --render (the INTERNAL scene size) stays unset so it follows the surface. The SURFACE size, however, must be pushed: gst-wayland-display neither sends a real xdg_toplevel.configure size nor honours set_fullscreen, so a client that asks the compositor comes up at winit's 800x600 default in the corner of the output (live-observed 2026-08-18, ~79% of every encoded frame static black). The launcher therefore derives --surface from QUASAR_STREAM_WIDTH/HEIGHT (quasar#384) exactly like every other image in this repo; BENCHAPP_SURFACE overrides it. BENCHAPP_MARKER_SCALE is pinned to 0.5 because the app's own 1.0 default puts a 960x608 high-contrast block on a 1080p frame (28% of the area) and would dominate every encoder-difficulty measurement; 0.5 still decodes with a valid CRC after a 1080p->720p downscale at 2 Mbps. Telemetry lands in the managed home under ~/benchapp/run-<ts>/{frames,events}.jsonl + summary.json (with ~/benchapp/latest symlinked to the current run) and a [benchapp] status line is printed to container stdout once per second. Rebuilt 2026-08-19 against quasar-benchgame 946da34 (adds commit_ms, CLOCK_REALTIME immediately after wl_surface.commit) — see images/quasar-benchapp/README.md "Known builds".
